s1.syndrome_frame: a clinical presentation of respiratory symptoms with a mass in the lung and an expansile lesion in the hyoid bone
salient_findings: a 3.1 × 2.7 × 3.6 cm mass in the right lower lobe
an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified 4.1 × 2.3 × 2.8 cm expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone
key_facts: 27-year-old man
history of a 5 mm‐thick melanoma on his posterior neck treated six years earlier
presented with hemoptysis and dyspnea
vital signs were within normal limits
physical examination was notable only for scattered breath sounds without stridor
laboratory studies, including complete blood count and metabolic panel, were unremarkable
contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed a mass in the right lower lobe
endobronchial ultrasound–guided fine-needle aspiration of the lung lesion demonstrated a malignant small round blue cell tumor
molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation
PET/CT showed an FDG-avid right lower lobe mass and an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone
ultrasound–guided core needle biopsy of the hyoid lesion was nondiagnostic
mid-treatment PET/CT demonstrated a substantial decrease in size and complete metabolic response of the lung mass but development of right neck adenopathy and interval growth of the hyoid bone lesion

raw.rationale: Molecular studies were interpreted as consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET) and the patient's response to chemotherapy typical for Ewing sarcoma

rejected.label: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor
rejected.why: Although molecular studies suggested PNET, Ewing sarcoma is a more specific diagnosis that encompasses PNET and better explains the clinical presentation

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and biopsy results do not support a diagnosis of plasmacytoma, which typically presents with different clinical and pathological features

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and imaging studies do not support a diagnosis of chondrosarcoma, which typically presents with a distinct cartilaginous matrix on imaging

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and biopsy results do not support a diagnosis of osteosarcoma, which typically presents with a distinct osteoid matrix on imaging and biopsy
